stories.title: Court asked to order Élections Québec to mail out English voting information
stories.summary: Montreal - A lawyer is asking a judge to order Élections Québec to mail out voter information in both French and English, after the elections agency said earlier this month that it would be providing the documents in French only.
stories.author: Morgan Lowrie The Canadian Press
stories.content:
MONTREAL - A lawyer for Élections Québec told a Montreal courtroom on Thursday that there might be time to send out one piece of English-language voter information by mail, as the elections agency and provincial government faced a court challenge over French-only mailouts.

Sept. 10, 2026

Updated at 6:30 p.m.

JJF[](http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/quebec/court-asked-to-order-lections-qu-bec-to-mail-out-english-voting-information/article_17857d50-4d20-5a4e-9223-6d6b85164300.html)

By Morgan Lowrie The Canadian Press

But Henrick Lavoie also told a Quebec Superior Court judge that it’s too late to send out both an English version of a voting guide and an English notice card to electors before the Oct. 5 vote.

“I submit respectfully that it’s impossible, downright impossible,” he said in a Montreal courtroom.

ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW

Who’s downloading photos of your kid at dance competitions?

Image 9Image 10Image 11

However, he said it might still be possible to send out a voting reminder card in English if the court issues an order to that effect by Sept. 16. The list of candidates is finalized at 2 p.m. on Sept. 17 and the agency had already planned to print out reminder cards to mail out after that deadline.

He said the additional cards printed in English would cost the province about $6 million.

Élections Québec is being pressed to address the issue after Montreal lawyer Doug Mitchell took it to court, seeking an order that would force the provincial agency to send out voter information in both French and English.

The agency said earlier this month that it would be providing the documents in French only.

Mitchell told the court that not giving people the information they need to cast a ballot could hurt their ability to exercise their right to vote.

“The end result of this, if no documents are sent, is that the people wanting to vote will be denied the right to vote because they will not have had the ability to understand and act to advance their interests to exercise one of the most fundamental rights in the world,” he said.

Élections Québec said on Sept. 1 that printed voter cards will be available only in French for the first time in its history, in order to comply with new language legislation.

The provincial elections authority said it must follow legislation adopted in 2022 making French the sole language of communication for public institutions, but said the documents will include a QR code for voters seeking online information in English.

Mitchell noted that Élections Québec sought an exemption to the law in order to be allowed to mail information in both languages, but was denied.

He cited a letter written to the Quebec government by the province’s chief electoral officer that suggested the validity of the election could be challenged if it were forced to apply the law to the letter.

“That the government of Quebec would prefer to take the risk of an election being invalidated or annulled (rather) than provide the documents that the (elections agency) believes are necessary for a fair election … the court should be troubled by that,” Mitchell said.

He said the QR code isn’t an adequate substitute because many people can’t access them, including some seniors and people without cellphones or reliable internet.

Mitchell, acting on behalf of plaintiff Geoffrey Chambers, asked the judge to grant an emergency order to get the elections agency to provide English copies of the provincial election guide, a notice sent to electors, and a reminder card.

Éric Cantin, the lawyer for the Quebec government, on the other hand, argued that the obligation to inform voters does not equal a right to mailed documents in English. Cantin noted that Élections Québec has several other ways of delivering information to voters, including through English ads, the media, a phone line and online.

“What we’re trying to invent is a right to a mailing by post, and not a right to information because the information is there,” he said.

He said a ruling in Mitchell’s favour would amount to creating an “absolute obligation” to send material in both French and English. “And what else? What’s to stop it from continuing after that — and being sent out in every language — if you start putting that kind of thing forward?” he said.

Cantin also argued that it is up to the Quebec government to draft language laws, and to address issues with them.

That last assertion drew pushback from Superior Court Justice Sylvain Lussier, who noted that a government representing the majority can’t always be trusted to advocate for minority rights.

“When you say ‘trust the legislator,’ I’m not reassured,” he said.

Lussier also questioned Mitchell on why, by his logic, speakers of other languages shouldn’t also be able to insist to have voting information mailed to them in their first language.

Mitchell said the case hinged not only on whether a right is being violated, but also on whether the restriction could be justified. He said that wasn’t the case at present, especially since Élections Québec had itself argued for the importance of continuing to provide English documents.

Lussier took notice of Élections Québec’s cutoff date to produce the reminder cards, but did not say when he would issue a decision.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 10, 2026.

The Canadian Press

stories.title: Trump's Canada-bashing echoed by supporters at Dallas convention
stories.summary: Dallas - Thousands of U.S. President Donald Trump's most ardent followers have gathered in Dallas for "Trump-a-Palooza" this week and many are parroting the president's constant bashing of Canada.
stories.author: Kelly Geraldine Malone The Canadian Press
stories.content:
DALLAS - Thousands of U.S. President Donald Trump’s most ardent followers gathered in Dallas for “Trump-a-palooza” this week — and many parroted the president’s constant bashing of Canada.

Sept. 10, 2026

Updated at 11:25 p.m.

JE[](http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/trump-s-canada-bashing-echoed-by-supporters-at-dallas-convention/article_ebd67172-111a-5d46-bfa2-6bb8c066aa84.html)

By Kelly Geraldine Malone The Canadian Press

Lona Heins from Tennessee said Canada was “communist” and no longer shared the same values as the United States.

“It’s contentious. I think Canada is socialist. It’s much, much more socialist,” she said. “I’m not even going to say that word anymore. It’s communist. We share different values now.”

ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW

Who’s downloading photos of your kid at dance competitions?

Like many Trump supporters at the unusual two-day Republican midterm convention, Heins spoke highly of Canadians and said she knows many people north of the border.

Heins, 58, said she was raised in South Dakota with family in North Dakota and Canadians were like family.

“What I see in Canada is not the Canada I remember growing up,” she said.

She said her change in opinion didn’t come from bilateral trade tensions, which she wants to see resolved. She said she needed more information before speaking about the trade dispute.

“I wish that there was a way for them to fix it but I stand with my president,” she said. “I’m here for Donald J. Trump. It makes me sad but I hope there’s a way they can come to an agreement.”

Trump on Tuesday escalated the trade war with Canada, signing executive orders to ban a range of Canadian exports and shuffle tariffs on others. Most imports of Canadian liquor, motorcycles, and a handful of dairy products are to be banned from the United States by the end of September.

Tensions between the countries grew after trade talks broke down in August. In response, Trump slapped an array of Canadian goods with 50 per cent duties. Canada responded with retaliatory tariffs earlier this week.

While headlining the midterm convention, Trump talked Wednesday about his move to rename Lake Ontario to “Lake America” and said Canada “very much” wanted a trade deal.

The president was more subdued in his comments about the United States’ northern neighbour, which he’s threatened to annex for nearly two years. He didn’t mention the country during his Thursday address.

Canada stayed off the list of issues most of Thursday, even when Republican Mike Rogers, who is in a must-watch Senate race for a Michigan seat against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, took the stage.

Rogers’ speech didn’t mention Canada, despite the impact of the trade war on deeply integrated industries in his state, particularly autos.

El-Sayed, meanwhile, has made Canada a ballot-box issue. Last week, he said, “this vanity war is not a war with Canada.”

“It’s a war on Michigan because we have to pay the price,” he said. “And we pay it every single day for goods that should not cost as much as they do.”

Recent polling suggests Trump’s tariffs and his move to rename Lake Ontario have been widely unpopular ahead of the critical November midterm elections.

Trump’s anti-Canada rhetoric seems to be seeping down to his followers.

Gallup polling published in March shows Canada’s favourable rating among Republicans has fallen to 62 per cent, down from 85 per cent in 2025.

Matthew Lebo, a political-science professor at Western University in London, Ont., said that in an increasingly polarized United States, voters are likely to look to their political leaders and adopt their opinions, even if they go against their own interests.

“When the leader of a political party, and somebody that 20 to 30 per cent of people are totally devoted to, says that Canada plays dirty and that they are unfair and they’ve been taking advantage of us for ages and all that, then the people who listen to them are going to believe that,” Lebo said.

On the flip side, Lebo said Trump’s overt hostility toward Canada also shores up the opinions of people who don’t like him. Gallup polling shows around 95 per cent of Democrats rate Canada positively.

Democrat senators, including Foreign Relations Committee ranking member Jeanne Shaheen, issued a statement Wednesday saying Trump was doubling down on a “senseless trade war.”

The senators, who represent states that rely on Canada as a key trading partner and export market, said the tariff war was raising costs for families and businesses.

“Congressional Republicans need to stand up to the president and do their part to give families and businesses on both sides of the border relief from this insanity,” the statement said.

Lebo said the shifting opinions about Canada among Republicans stem from Trump’s most faithful supporters putting their complete trust in what the president says.

It doesn’t necessarily come from an understanding of current issues between Canada and the United States, he added.

Asked about Canada-U.S. trade tensions, rally attendee MaryAnn Miron said Canadians ought to get rid of Justin Trudeau — who announced his resignation as prime minister in January 2025 and was replaced by Mark Carney in March of that year.

“I feel sorry for you all with Trudeau,” she said.

“You guys are in a crappy situation and he needs to be outted. And I think a lot of that is going to help solve the problem between the countries, but I wish you guys the best.”

When told that Trudeau was no longer prime minister, Miron said, “I haven’t been watching the news.”

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 10, 2026.

The Canadian Press

stories.title: Poilievre tells U.S. audience Canadians are feeling 'wounded' from U.S. trade actions
stories.summary: Pierre Poilievre was in New York City on Thursday, urging Americans to return to two-way tariff-free trade between Canada and the U.S.
stories.author: Jordan Gowling
stories.content:
The Conservative leader urged the U.S. administration and Congress to knock down tariffs

Ottawa — Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre was in New York City on Thursday, urging Americans to return to two-way tariff-free trade between Canada and the U.S.

“Let’s knock down those tariffs and focus on building a stronger North America for our two separate countries,” said Poilievre, during an interview on Cnbc’s Squawk Box.

Poilievre is visiting the U.S. to promote free trade and participate in ceremonies commemorating the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks. The leader of the opposition was also asked about Canadians’ feelings towards the U.S.

“Look, I think we feel a little bit wounded,” said Poilievre. “We’re kind of confused as to how it is suddenly that Canada ended up in the crosshairs.”

The Conservative leader urged the U.S. administration and Congress to knock down tariffs, adding that the trade war between Canada and the U.S. should have been “over yesterday.”

When asked whether trust can be restored between the two countries, Poilievre said it would start with the removal of tariffs.

“Because as soon as that happens, then I think we can work together,” said Poilievre. “At the same time, Canada is beginning to diversify, further diversify its trade to overseas markets, and that is going to be necessary now, regardless of what the administration does.”

The trade conflict between the U.S. and Canada has intensified in recent weeks , following the collapse in trade negotiations between both sides last month. U.S. President Donald Trump then imposed a 50 per-cent tariff on nearly $28 billion of Canadian goods, with Canada matching those tariffs, imposing levies ranging from 15 to 50 per cent on $27.6 billion worth of U.S. imports this week.

On Tuesday, Trump announced he would impose import bans on some Canadian alcohol products, dairy products and motorcycles. Economists have said the impact from the bans will be minimal on the Canadian economy.

Trump has also taken issue with the loonie’s exchange rate with the U.S. dollar and has threatened to ban aircraft maker Bombardier from selling in the U.S. The president also intends to impose a 50 per-cent tariff on Canadian autos and trucks on Jan. 1.

On Thursday, Carney was asked why he thinks Trump is so angry with Canada.

“I can’t look deeply into the souls of other people and see their emotions,” said Carney, during a press conference in Calgary, alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. “T his isn’t a question of emotion, it’s a question of sovereignty.”

Carney said he had spoken with the president in recent days about the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. He also reiterated that Canada stands ready to strike a “fair” trade deal with the Americans.

stories.title: N.B. premier directing public institutions to stop buying American amid trade war
stories.summary: Fredericton - New Brunswick Premier Susan Holt has ordered the province’s public sector to stop buying American products when Canadian substitutes are available, saying the move is in response to the latest round of U.S. tariffs.
stories.author: The Canadian Press
stories.content:
FREDERICTON - New Brunswick Premier Susan Holt has ordered the province’s public sector to stop buying American products when Canadian substitutes are available, saying the move is in response to the latest round of U.S. tariffs.

Sept. 10, 2026

Updated at 5:45 p.m.

EJR[](http://www.thestar.com/news/canada/new-brunswick/n-b-premier-directing-public-institutions-to-stop-buying-american-amid-trade-war/article_4f8ace5b-346a-5195-8f8e-80e18194de3d.html)

By The Canadian Press

As well, Holt announced Thursday that her government will ban the purchase of U.S. goods and services for government contracts valued at more than $5 million, starting Oct. 1. That limit will cover about 90 per cent of government contracts handled by Service New Brunswick, she said.

The measures come after U.S. President Donald Trump announced Tuesday a ban on imports of some Canadian products, including alcohol and motorcycles, and new 50 per cent tariffs on other products.

ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW

Who’s downloading photos of your kid at dance competitions?

“We can’t control what President Trump does, but we can control what we do here in New Brunswick,” Holt said.

“We’ve seen this movie before. When you put a tax on products coming across the border, someone pays that bill, and too often, that somebody is a family sitting around their kitchen table trying to make ends meet.”

On another front, Holt said her government will determine if it has the authority to prevent Americans from obtaining fishing and hunting licences, as well as staking mining claims.

“This is a negotiating tool that creates a significant response among ... influential Americans,” she said, referring specifically to hunting and fishing licences.

“And we also know that New Brunswickers love their moose licences, and if we can get a few more of those into the hands of New Brunswickers, I think they’d appreciate that opportunity.”

The premier also announced a long list of compensation, training and employee retention programs for New Brunswick businesses affected by the trade war. She said the province will also launch a market diversification strategy, as well as a renewed buy-local campaign.

“When you have the choice, we’re asking you to choose New Brunswick and Canadian products,” Holt said.

In February 2025, Holt directed the provincial Crown corporation NB Liquor to stop buying U.S. alcohol and remove all American products from its shelves, as did most other provinces. At the time, the New Brunswick government also started reviewing its procurement policies.

On Thursday, Holt said that in the 2025-26 fiscal year, her government cut its spending on U.S. contracts from $34.4 million to $16.4 million. That reduced the amount of contracts going to American suppliers from 1.4 per cent to 0.7 of the $2 billion spent on contracts.

In January, the province starting selling off its remaining stock of U.S. booze, but Holt announced Thursday that NB Liquor would stop marketing American brands and begin giving priority to Canadian products.

Canadian Manufacturers & Exporters, a national trade group, said it supports buying local but said the priority should be de-escalation and a return to a “stable, predictable trading relationship.”

“Any response should be carefully targeted to avoid raising costs or further disrupting the integrated supply chains that support workers and businesses on both sides of the border,” said Dennis Darby, the organization’s president and CEO, in a statement.

This report by Canadian Press was first published Sept. 10, 2026.

— By Tori Fitzpatrick in Halifax

stories.title: Canada’s housing supply gap narrowly improves, but pace of construction could slow, Cmhc says
stories.summary: Between 417,000 and 469,000 new housing units needed per year to restore affordability, federal housing agency says
stories.author: Sammy Hudes
stories.content:
The federal housing agency says Canada narrowly chipped away at its supply gap over the past year, but the country still needs up to nearly 4.7 million new homes over the next decade to restore prepandemic affordability by 2036.

Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp. released its latest supply gap estimate report, which said between 417,000 and 469,000 new housing units are needed a year across the ownership and rental markets over the next decade to reach affordability targets.

That’s down slightly from its last estimate in July, 2025, when CMHC said the pace of home construction would need to roughly double to between 430,000 and 480,000 new units annually over the coming decade.

But the agency says recent affordability gains are at risk as new home construction is instead expected to slow, especially in the home ownership market.

CMHC deputy chief economist Aled ab Iorwerth says housing costs have come down overall, citing slower population growth, but the “key risk now is Canada underbuilds during this softer market and finds itself further short of housing when demand strengthens again.”

Since the agency’s previous estimates, it says the housing supply gap has narrowed in Toronto, remained stable in Vancouver, and grown larger in Montreal and Ottawa. Meanwhile, record housing construction in Calgary has narrowed its housing supply gap “significantly,” while Edmonton remains the only large market in Canada without a housing supply gap.

stories.title: Tornado confirmed in Winnipeg neighbourhood, another west of the city
stories.summary: The Northern Tornaodes Project confirmed two twisters landed in Manitoba on Sunday evening, including one in a Winnipeg neighbourhood.
stories.author: Tavi Dhillon
stories.content:
A tornado is confirmed to have landed in the River Heights neighbourhood of Winnipeg during Sunday’s storm , according to the Northern Tornadoes Project (NTP).

The EF1 twister occurred in Winnipeg at 6:31 p.m. that day, the NTP said, noting that another tornado occurred around less than an hour earlier approximately 50 kilometres outside of the city in Bénard, Man.

The River Heights tornado tracked through two kilometres of the suburb, with winds peaking at 155 km/h, Dave Sills, director of the NTP said. No injuries were reported in the River Heights tornado, but NTP surveyors noted damage to shingles on the roofs of homes in the neighbourhood, as well as on sheds and trees.

“We saw a car that was moved, and that doesn’t happen with a weaker kind of wind or an EF0 tornado. Certainly, you’d need stronger winds for that,” Sills told Global News, adding that the car’s movement was “an indication that the winds were fairly strong with this tornado.”

The Bénard twister was also classified as an EF1, with peak winds estimated at 165 km/h.

One injury was reported in the Bénard tornado after a garage door was blown into someone, he said, adding that the extent of their injuries is unknown.

NTP ground and drone surveys were also said to have identified damage to several buildings and grain bins at a large farm property.

Looking to the upcoming autumn season, Sills said the tornado forecast is unclear – especially with a super El Niño expected to hit in the second half of this year, and an unusually high tornado count.

Manitoba has seen 15 twisters in 2026, two of which were within Winnipeg city limits, according to the group’s director.

stories.title: Canada will help to rebuild Ukraine when Russia’s war ends, Carney tells Zelensky
stories.summary: Prime Minister also says Canada supports ‘Ukraine’s path to joining Nato’ and the European Union
stories.author: Dayne Patterson
stories.content:
Canada and Ukraine are deepening ties with the signing of what they are touting as a 100-year partnership to further co-operation in several areas, including defence, energy, technology and trade.

Amid heavy security in southeast Calgary on Thursday, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a series of industry alliances and non-binding agreements with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who is visiting Canada for three days to strengthen ties.

“This relationship has flourished for over a hundred years and it will flourish in the century ahead, long after this war ends,” Mr. Carney said. “Ukrainians helped build Canada, and Canadians will help rebuild Ukraine.”

Canada’s domestic defence industry stands to benefit from several of the partnerships. This includes a long-term government-to-government collaboration to jointly produce uncrewed systems, counterdrone technologies and munitions, which will combine Ukrainian expertise with Canadian manufacturing and technology.

Ukrainian President Volodomyr Zelensky met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ahead of a Liberal cabinet meeting in Alberta. Carney says the meeting will focus on the countries' shared priorities, including deepening defence, economic and energy co-operation.

The Canadian Press

Mr. Carney also committed to sending Ukraine one-third of all drones manufactured in Canada. Some of those could be produced through Ottawa’s new marketplace for uncrewed systems, which is meant to expedite the production and delivery of the low-cost technologies to the Canadian Armed Forces.

Finally, a Ukrainian-Canadian joint venture, also announced Thursday, will bring together General Dynamics Mission Systems-Canada, an Ottawa-based subsidiary of the U.S. defence giant, and Ukrainian company Green Tech Harvest to produce uncrewed systems for use in the war. A similar joint venture was established in May between Canadian drone company Sentinel R&D and Ukrainian drone company Airlogix.

“Together, we will build the capabilities our militaries need, create good jobs at home, support Ukraine on the battlefield and strengthen the sovereignty of both our nations,” Mr. Carney said.

Canada is also doubling down on its military and energy aid for Ukraine. Ottawa has committed almost $9-billion in military aid and $70-million to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund since Russia began its full-scale invasion in 2022.

Mr. Carney said the government intends to bump its support even further, with a $350-million equipment package of critical air-defence interceptors. It will come through the United States’ Joint Ukraine Multinational Program, which was set up to allow the rapid delivery of services, training and articles using financial donations from other countries.

Ottawa will also provide more than $430-million in loan guarantees for Ukrainians to buy gas throughout the winter, Mr. Carney said. Moscow has pummelled much of the country’s critical infrastructure, leading to energy shortages and constant rolling blackouts.

Mr. Zelensky thanked Canada for its continuing support, saying, “We need strong friends.”

The two leaders also pointed to Canada’s intention over the coming months to join and support Ukraine’s low-cost ballistic missile shield, Freya, to contribute to European air defence.

“The biggest threat and the biggest challenge for us is ballistic attacks, and the most important thing is air defence,” Mr. Zelensky said.

Thursday’s agreements were inked ahead of Mr. Zelensky’s planned meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump in New York later this month to discuss the war. The prospect of Ukraine’s entry into the North Atlantic Treaty Organization remains on indefinite hold, being proffered as a bargaining chip by U.S. officials in peace talks with Russia.

If Moscow undermines those negotiations, Ottawa is prepared to increase pressure on it and is developing a new package of sanctions focused on anti-ballistic missile capabilities, Mr. Carney said.

He said Canada is also updating its existing sanctions on Russia’s financial services and its shadow fleet of oil tankers transporting goods and commodities around the world.

Peace, however, remains the ultimate goal.

“We need to end this war,” Mr. Zelensky said. “We don’t have any kind of alternative.”

The announcement in Calgary was part of a three-day trip to Canada by Mr. Zelensky and his wife, Olena Zelenska. They arrived in the city Wednesday night, and later Thursday they headed to Banff where Mr. Zelensky addressed a federal cabinet meeting. He and his wife are also scheduled to visit Toronto and North Bay before leaving Canada on Friday.

Prime Minister Mark Carney and his cabinet are swapping Parliament for the picturesque Rocky Mountains this week, but the agenda for the cabinet retreat in Banff is packed. As Marieke Walsh reports, the intensifying trade war with the United States and Alberta's upcoming separation referendum are both top of mind.

The Globe and Mail

stories.title: Newfoundland and Labrador to lead economic growth in 2026, Ontario to lag: report
stories.summary: Ottawa — A new report says Newfoundland and Labrador is expected to lead the country's economic growth for a second year in a row, driven by higher crude prices and offshore oil projects.
stories.author: News Staff
stories.content:
OTTAWA — Canada’s economic growth is expected to rebound later this year and into 2027 as hiring activity strengthens and business confidence recovers, Signal49 Research said Thursday.

In its provincial five-year outlook, the Ottawa-based think tank formerly known as the Conference Board of Canada said the momentum is supported by stronger public and private investments, steady gains in consumer spending and an assumed easing of Canada-U.S. trade tensions.

Yet escalating tariffs, the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and looming demographic pressures are creating uncertainty and significant headwinds for the Canadian economy, the independent research organization said.

“Business investment has been really weak in Canada recently, but we’re seeing some signs that that could be turning around,” said Richard Forbes, principal economist at Signal49 Research. “It is coming from a very low level but it’s starting to turn the corner, so it is optimistic.”

Still, the trade war remains a significant risk to the country’s economic growth prospects, he said.

“The longer it gets drawn out, the more it escalates, the worse the outlook is going to be for Canada,” Forbes said.

Despite the slightly rosier outlook in the latter half of the year, the economic picture varies considerably by province, with different regions feeling the effects of economic headwinds and tailwinds differently, the think tank said.

The two key standouts are Newfoundland and Labrador and Ontario, which sit at opposite ends of the provincial economic outlook ranking.

Newfoundland and Labrador is expected to lead the country’s economic expansion for the second year in a row, driven by higher crude prices and offshore oil projects, the report said.

The province’s economy will expand 3.7 per cent in 2026, though longer-term growth will be constrained by demographic pressures, it predicted.

“Oil production has really been the driver of Newfoundland and Labrador this year,” Forbes said. “But over the longer term it is one of the weakest-growth provinces because it has a more senior population and trouble attracting migrants.”

Ontario is expected to post the softest growth this year, with the economy expanding just 0.2 per cent, the research organization said.

The country’s most populous province has been one of the hardest hit by U.S. tariffs, largely due to its manufacturing sector, it said.

“The auto sector has been continually targeted since early 2025 and almost 100 per cent of Canadian auto production is in Ontario,” Forbes said.

Quebec’s economy is challenged by its broad exposure to tariffs and slow population growth, but is expected to grow 0.7 per cent in 2026 amid a predicted rebound in exports, employment and investment, Signal49 Research said.

In British Columbia, population growth will be constrained by a tight housing supply and high cost of living, the think tank said.

However, LNG developments, strong trade prospects with Asia and the province’s relative insulation from the U.S. trade dispute will support B.C.’s economy, which is forecasted to grow 1.4 per cent in 2026, it said.

In Alberta, the resource sector and a growing artificial intelligence industry will support the province’s economy in 2026 and 2027, Signal49 Research said.

The province is expected to see strong job creation and robust business investment, with the economy forecasted to grow 1.5 per cent in 2026 and remaining one of Canada’s strongest performers over the coming decade, it said.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 10, 2026.

Brett Bundale, The Canadian Press

stories.title: London man dies, another critically injured in crash near Woodstock
stories.summary: The collision involved a pickup truck and an SUV.
stories.author: Brian Williams
stories.content:
The aftermath of a crash involving a pickup truck and an SUV at Cassel Sideroad and Highway 59 in East Zorra-Tavistock on Thursday, Sept. 10, 2026. (OPP photo)

A 50-year-old London man is dead and another person remains in serious condition after a two-vehicle collision northwest of Woodstock, police say.

Shortly before 5:15 a.m. Thursday, OPP officers, along with Oxford County firefighters and paramedics, were called to a crash involving a pickup truck and an SUV at Cassel Sideroad and Highway 59 – a rural intersection about 15 kilometres northwest of Woodstock – in East Zorra-Tavistock township, OPP said in a news release.

The lone occupant of the SUV, a 50-year-old London man, was taken to hospital, where he later died of his injuries, OPP said. The lone occupant of the pickup truck remains in hospital with life-threatening injuries.

“We will provide an update on that individual once we’re updated on their condition,” OPP Const. Randi Crawford said.

Highway 59 between Cassel Sideroad and Maplewood Sideroad is closed while police, with assistance from the West Region OPP traffic incident management and enforcement team, investigate the crash, the release said.

Crawford said the cause of the crash hasn’t been determined.

“Anytime that there is a collision involving a fatal, those trained professionals will be there, and they will do a thorough investigation to find out what in fact, the cause of the collision was.”

The area where the crash occurred is a “very busy area” in Oxford County, Crawford said. When The Free Press spoke with Crawford around 10:45 a.m., she said the OPP hoped to have the area cleared within two hours.

Investigators have said the accused and victims had all lived in the encampment in recent years.

stories.title: Canada needs up to 4.69 million new homes by 2036, but construction could slow: Cmhc
stories.summary: The federal housing agency says Canada narrowly chipped away at its supply gap over the past year, but the country still needs up to nearly 4.7 million new homes over the next decade to restore pre-pandemic affordability by 2036.
stories.author: News Staff
stories.content:
By Sammy Hudes, The Canadian Press

Posted September 10, 2026 11:15 am.

Last Updated September 10, 2026 12:07 pm.

The federal housing agency says Canada narrowly chipped away at its supply gap over the past year, but the country still needs up to nearly 4.7 million new homes over the next decade to restore pre-pandemic affordability by 2036.

Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp. released its latest supply gap estimate report, which said between 417,000 and 469,000 new housing units are needed per year across the ownership and rental markets over the next decade to reach affordability targets.

That’s down slightly from its last estimate in July 2025, when Cmhc said the pace of home construction would need to roughly double to between 430,000 and 480,000 new units annually over the coming decade.

But the agency warned recent affordability gains are at risk as new home construction is instead expected to slow, especially in the home ownership market.

“Although slower population growth has brought some improvements in affordability, new construction is slowing faster than demand,” Cmhc deputy chief economist Aled ab Iorwerth said in a news release.

“The key risk now is Canada underbuilds during this softer market and finds itself further short of housing when demand strengthens again.”

A total of 131,851 housing starts have been recorded so far this year through July, down four per cent from the same seven-month period in 2025.

At the current pace of housing construction, Canada is on track to add around 231,000 housing units per year over the next decade, according to the report, around half the annual pace needed to reach the 2019 affordability levels by 2036.

The agency defines affordability as the share of income that goes toward housing. In general, it aims to return to levels of affordability at which adjusted house prices are no higher than 30 per cent of average gross household income.

The report said meeting future housing demand will depend on the pace of new construction. But the sector is facing pressure from high construction costs, while presale financing conditions remain difficult for some projects. Weak condominium market conditions are also making developers cautious about launching new projects.

“Housing supply needs will increase over the long term. Population growth is expected to recover across most major cities, and rising incomes will support housing demand,” the report said.

“As a result, there will be a need for more homes. Some households May have delayed forming because of affordability challenges. As conditions improve further, some of this suppressed demand will re-emerge.”

While Cmhc said the national supply gap is broadly unchanged from the assessment last year, there are key differences across regional markets.

Since the agency’s previous estimates, it said the housing supply gap has narrowed in Toronto, as lower home prices have improved affordability. However, new construction activity has weakened “sharply,” particularly in the condo market, limiting ownership housing supply.

The gap has remained stable in Vancouver, where improved affordability and stronger construction levels have been offset by slower future supply growth and population pressures.

Record housing construction in Calgary has narrowed that city’s housing supply gap by almost half, the report said, however affordability challenges remain, especially for lower-income households and prospective homeowners. Elsewhere in the province, Edmonton remains the only large market in Canada without a housing supply gap “because housing construction has generally kept pace with population growth.”

But the gap has grown larger in both Montreal and Ottawa compared with a year ago. In Montreal, housing construction levels remain high, the report said, but new supply is concentrated in rental housing, while weak condo supply is limiting ownership options.

Similar challenges persist in the country’s capital city, where affordability has deteriorated, Cmhc said.

“We expect housing demand to grow faster than the housing supply despite strong construction activity,” it said of Ottawa.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 10, 2026.

Sammy Hudes, The Canadian Press

stories.title: Windsor council candidate calls Zionists 'terrorists' and 'serial killers'
stories.summary: Windsor city council candidate is facing fallout over remarks calling Zionists "terrorists" and "serial killers" who should be locked up.
stories.author: Derek Spalding
stories.content:
Canada

Rasha Zaid said her opposition to Zionism should not be interpreted as hostility toward Jewish people

Rasha Zaid, an organizer with the Windsor4Palestine organization is shown on Thursday, January 23, 2025.Photo by Dan Janisse /Windsor Star

A Windsor city council candidate is facing fallout over public remarks referring to Zionists as “terrorists” and “serial killers” who should be locked up, comments that have drawn attention well beyond the city as the municipal election campaign gets underway.

Rasha Zaid, one of five candidates seeking the Ward 4 council seat in the Oct. 26 election, made the statements during a protest in Windsor. Video of the speech has since circulated online and the controversy has attracted international attention, including coverage by the Jerusalem Post.

“Every person that announced that they’re Zionists must be locked up,” Zaid says in one video clip. “They should all be locked up. They’re terrorists.”

The next issue of NP Posted will soon be in your inbox.

We encountered an issue signing you up. Please try again

In a second clip Zaid goes on to say, “t hey are nothing but serial killers on the loose, and they must be held accountable.”

The Windsor Jewish Federation and Community Centre said broad comments like these risk leaving people feeling targeted because of their beliefs or identity. Officials issued a statement saying Zionism broadly refers to the belief that Jewish people have a right to self-determination in their ancestral homeland and does not necessarily mean support for any particular Israeli government, policy or military action.

“Because many Jewish people consider Zionism part of their identity or connection to Israel, comments directed broadly at ‘Zionists’ can have a significant impact on members of the Jewish community,” the federation said in a statement. “Members of our community have expressed concern that rhetoric of this nature contributes to an increasingly difficult environment and makes some people more cautious about openly expressing their Jewish identity.”

In an interview, Zaid said her opposition to Zionism should not be interpreted as hostility toward Jewish people.

“Zionism and Judaism are not the same thing, and the constant conflation of the two must truly be put to an end,” she said. “One is a faith, and one is a political ideology.”

Zaid said she does not object to Jewish self-determination but opposes actions she believes have been carried out under the banner of Zionism.

“I’m vocally anti-Zionist for many reasons, for what has been done and what has been carried out under the political ideology of Zionism,” she said.

Asked whether she believes merely identifying as a Zionist should be grounds for imprisonment, Zaid said that was not her position.

“I didn’t say if you have a political ideology of Zionism, you should be locked up,” she said, adding that her comments were directed at people responsible for war crimes.

Online criticism, though, points to how her words captured on video were broader: “Every person that announced that they’re Zionists must be locked up.”

But Zaid said the circulating video was a short excerpt taken from a much longer speech at a Windsor protest and did not provide the context surrounding her remarks.

“When somebody takes bits and pieces of an entire speech to only fit a certain narrative, that is not honest journalism,” she said. “It completely changes it around. It’s not fair.”

Zaid also rejected equating anti-Zionism with antisemitism, saying many Jewish people are anti-Zionist and, “criticizing political ideology does not mean you’re antisemitic.”

She wants to put the latest discussions about her protests behind her and instead focus on her campaign and municipal issues, such as building affordable housing, boosting the local economy and ethical spending, and creating safe spaces and an active community.

“I honestly will no longer be answering any questions regarding this matter (about Zionism comments) because I think I’ve made my point very clear, many, many, many times,” she said.

Zaid is running against Mike Burton, Catherine Gariepy-Schulze, Chris Holt and Xsander Moisenko for the Ward 4 council seat.

Rasha Zaid, an organizer with the Windsor4Palestine organization is shown on Thursday, January 23, 2025.Photo by Dan Janisse /Windsor Star

A Windsor city council candidate is facing fallout over public remarks referring to Zionists as “terrorists” and “serial killers” who should be locked up, comments that have drawn attention well beyond the city as the municipal election campaign gets underway.

Rasha Zaid, one of five candidates seeking the Ward 4 council seat in the Oct. 26 election, made the statements during a protest in Windsor. Video of the speech has since circulated online and the controversy has attracted international attention, including coverage by the Jerusalem Post.
“Every person that announced that they’re Zionists must be locked up,” Zaid says in one video clip. “They should all be locked up. They’re terrorists.”

stories.title: Buffalo Bills recruit Barenaked Ladies to play O Canada at home opener
stories.summary: The Nfl's Buffalo Bills have enlisted Canadian rock band Barenaked Ladies to perform O Canada at the team's home opener this month.
stories.author: Kenn Oliver
stories.content:
Canada

The NFL club is owned by Terry and Kim Pegula, proprietors of the NHL's Buffalo Sabres, a club that's played the Canadian anthem at every home game since 1970

Last updated 13 minutes ago[](http://nationalpost.com/news/Canada/buffalo-bills-barenaked-ladies-o-Canada-home-opener#comments-area)

The Nfl's Buffalo Bills have enlisted Canadian rock band Barenaked Ladies to perform O Canada at the team's home opener this month.Photo by Contributed/Barenaked Ladies

When the Buffalo Bills christen their new US$2.2 billion football stadium later this month, they’ll pay tribute to the city’s long-standing affinity for its Canadian neighbours on the other side of the Peace Bridge by performing O Canada along with the U.S. national anthem.

“For the first time in Highmark Stadium history, we will celebrate the American and Canadian anthems during pregame,” the Buffalo Bills shared on X Wednesday, highlighting Canada’s Barenaked Ladies as performers for the latter.

Auliʻi Cravalho, who voices Moana in the Disney movies of the same name, will sing the Star-Spangled Banner at the Sept. 17 game against the Detroit Lions.

National Post has inquired whether the organization intends to play the anthem at every regular-season game or just the home opener.

The Bills are owned by Terry and Kim Pegula, also proprietors of the NHL’s Buffalo Sabres, a club that has performed O Canada at every home game — even those that didn’t feature a Canadian team. The practice began upon the team’s founding in 1970, as a nod to the many fans co-owner Seymour Knox III knew they would attract from the nearby lower Niagara and St. Catharines area in Ontario.

When anthem singer Cami Clune’s microphone failed during a playoff game earlier this year, the Sabres faithful were quick to pick up the anthem and sing it to completion.

Fun fact: the Sabres were named by a Canadian — Toronto filmmaker Harry Cole, who entered and won a 1969 contest to name the team — and Knox said he specifically chose the Canadian English spelling of the word to honour the Canadian fans, according toThe Hockey Writers. (The swords are sabers in the U.S.)

Minor league baseball team the Buffalo Bisons, the AAA affiliate of the Toronto Blue Jays, and the National Lacrosse League’s Buffalo Bandits also perform O Canada before home games.

stories.title: London man killed Thursday morning in Oxford County crash
stories.summary: London man killed Thursday morning in Oxford County crash CBC
stories.author: CBC News
paragraphs: Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) in Oxford County say a 50-year-old London man is dead, and another driver is in hospital with life-threatening injuries, after a serious crash Thursday morning in East Zorra-Tavistock.
· Posted: Sep 10, 2026 10:54 AM EDT | Last Updated: 1 hour ago
Police say a section of Highway 59 northeast of London will be closed for several hours Thursday as they investigate a fatal crash.(Ontario Provincial Police)
Emergency crews were called to the intersection of Cassel Sideroad and Highway 59 at around 5:10 a.m., police said. The crash involved a pickup truck and an SUV.
The man driving the SUV was taken to hospital where he was later pronounced deceased. The driver of the pickup truck remains in hospital with life-threatening injuries.
Highway 59 will be closed for several hours between Cassel Sideroad and Maplewood Sideroad as police investigate the cause of the crash.
Anyone with information or video footage that could help with the investigation is asked to contact the OPP.

stories.title: Ottawa announces $5M for HIV self-test kits, support staff
stories.summary: Winnipeg - The federal government has announced $5 million in funding for HIV prevention and support services.
stories.author: Brittany Hobson The Canadian Press
stories.content:
“HIV is a manageable condition, and people living with HIV deserve to live healthy, full lives without stigma or discrimination,” Manitoba Liberal MP Doug Eyolfson announced Thursday.

“This funding is about making it easier for people to get tested, know their status, and access the care and support they need.”

ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW

Who’s downloading photos of your kid at dance competitions?

Image 9Image 10Image 11

Ottawa will provide $5 million to increase access to the kits and to hire peer-based support workers for communities facing the highest burdens of HIV. There is $2 million for the tests and $3 million for peer support networks.

The federal government says 2,300 new HIV diagnoses were reported in 2024, and an estimated 7,000 people live unaware they have HIV.

HIV, short for human immunodeficiency virus, attacks the immune system. Without treatment, it can weaken the body’s defences and progress to AIDS, which can be life-threatening.

Advocates say self-tests can be a way to overcome barriers — including racism and geography – that could prevent people from seeking help.

A breakdown of where the tests will be distributed is being finalized. Dr. Joss Reimer, Canada’s chief public health officer, said underserved communities are the priority.

“That would include community organizations working with Indigenous populations, men who have sex with men, Black communities and other racialized communities, and people who inject drugs,” Reimer said.

The Manitoba Harm Reduction Network, an advocacy group that works to reduce the transmission of sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections, said the self-tests are just the start and there needs to be followup help.

“Being able to access dignified care is also part of the plan,” said Shohan Illsley, the network’s executive director.

The issue is comparatively acute in Manitoba. In May, the province declared a public health emergency over HIV rates that it estimates are three times higher than the rest of Canada.

In 2024, the province reported a rate of 19.5 cases per 100,000. The national rate was about a quarter of that. The province said new cases have been increasing over the last six years, with 328 detected last year compared with 90 in 2019.

It called for more help from Ottawa to address the sharp rise in cases.

Uzoma Asagwara, Manitoba’s health minister, said Thursday’s announcement was a “big step” in addressing the issue but promised to continue to advocate for more investments.

The funding was welcomed by CATIE, an advocacy group that provides information on HIV and hepatitis C. It said it will help get Canada closer to its commitment to eliminate HIV as a public health concern by 2030.

“With Canada reporting a 23 per cent increase in estimated HIV infections, community-based workers have their work cut out for them,” said Jody Jollimore, executive director of CATIE.

“To keep the epidemic under control, we need long-term commitment.”

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 10, 2026.

The Canadian Press

stories.title: Ottawa announces $5 million for HIV self-test kits, more support staffers
stories.summary: Winnipeg — The federal government is dispatching 80,000 HIV self-test kits across Canada to expand access to HIV prevention.
stories.author: News Staff
stories.content:
The federal government is dispatching 80,000 HIV self-test kits across Canada to expand access to HIV prevention.

“HIV is a manageable condition, and people living with HIV deserve to live healthy, full lives without stigma or discrimination,” Manitoba Liberal MP Doug Eyolfson announced Thursday.

“This funding is about making it easier for people to get tested, know their status, and access the care and support they need.”

Ottawa will provide $5 million to increase access to the kits and to hire peer-based support workers for communities facing the highest burdens of HIV. There is $2 million for the tests and $3 million for peer support networks.

The federal government says 2,300 new HIV diagnoses were reported in 2024, and an estimated 7,000 people live unaware they have HIV.

HIV, short for human immunodeficiency virus, attacks the immune system. Without treatment, it can weaken the body’s defences and progress to AIDS, which can be life-threatening.

“That would include community organizations working with Indigenous populations, men who have sex with men, Black communities and other racialized communities, and people who inject drugs,” Reimer said.

The Manitoba Harm Reduction Network, an advocacy group that works to reduce the transmission of sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections, said the self-tests are just the start and there needs to be followup help.

“Being able to access dignified care is also part of the plan,” said Shohan Illsley, the network’s executive director.

The issue is comparatively acute in Manitoba. In May, the province declared a public health emergency over HIV rates that it estimates are three times higher than the rest of Canada.

In 2024, the province reported a rate of 19.5 cases per 100,000. The national rate was about a quarter of that. The province said new cases have been increasing over the last six years, with 328 detected last year compared with 90 in 2019.

stories.title: Are you willing to pay more to stand up to the U.S.? What readers told us
stories.summary: Global News asked its readers, 'Are you willing to pay higher prices or change brands in order to support the country's response to Trump's trade war?'
stories.author: Katie Scott
stories.content:
The United States escalated its trade war with Canada on Tuesday, announcing an upcoming ban on some Canadian dairy products and motorcycles as well as most alcoholic beverages after retaliatory Canadian counter-tariffs took effect on about $28 billion in U.S. goods.

Those counter-tariffs followed the U.S. imposing 50 per cent tariffs on Canada in August.

U.S. President Donald Trump also moved to shut Canadian products out of large, long-term U.S. government contracts.

The latest U.S. bans are set to take effect Sept. 29 and cover various Canadian wines and spirits, some motorcycles and mopeds, dairy products including whey and some types of molasses .

Canada’s tariffs on U.S. goods took effect at 10:01 a.m. Tuesday and hit hundreds of American products, including steel, aluminum, cheese, appliances, clothing, cosmetics and farm equipment, with rates of 15 per cent, 25 per cent or 50 per cent.

Eight of 10 Canadian provinces have already continued to restrict or ban sales of U.S. alcohol.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that Canada’s response is about reducing its dependence on the United States rather than simply weathering the latest tariffs.

“It’s about ensuring that no country can hold us hostage. And that we can live how we want to live,” he said.

As Canada’s counter-tariffs kick in, Global News asked its readers, “are you more or less determined to Buy Canadian? Are you willing to pay higher prices or change brands in order to support the country’s response to Trump’s trade war?”

These are some of your responses.

The vast majority of respondents said they would not be buying American products and will continue to Buy Canadian.

“Of course I am willing to pay more and continue to Buy Canadian. Although it will hit my pocket book harder, I believe that we have no other choice. Elbows up,” said one reader, Sallie.

Reader Denny said that they are “willing to support my country by paying higher prices to Buy Canadian.”

“As a retired Canadian, I am all in. I think it is time for Canada to make changes that have been required for decades to protect our nation from facing future trade wars as we are seeing in these current times. Our children and grandchildren are counting on it. Canada Strong,” said Bob M.

Reader Kim W. said she is “willing to do whatever it takes, including paying more for Canadian goods, to counter” Trump’s tariffs.

“My household is determined to avoid purchasing any U.S. product even if it means paying a little more for a Canadian product,” said Chris D.

Maureen H. said that the “retaliatory tariffs won’t hurt you if you don’t buy American.”

“Anything I haven’t found a substitute for, I do without. Hasn’t hurt me in the slightest,” she added.

“I will buy Canadian, so I hope more and more merchandise is made in Canada, from Canadian materials. I Refuse TO BUY ‘Made IN THE USA’. If this means paying a bit more for things, I will, gladly,” said reader Mary S.

James W. said he started “avoiding U.S. products during Trump’s first term and will most likely continue the rest of our lives.”

We’ll continue to buy Canadian first before buying products from countries that strongly support democracy,” he added.

Many readers also said they would be boycotting all things American, including travel.

“We have not and will not travel to the USA until a new leader who reverses all the tariffs is elected south of us. Where possible we have changed brands that are not American. Where possible we buy Canadian and then revert to Mexican Italian English. USA products are our last choice. Keep up the good work Mr Carney,” said Glenda C.

Reader Eric E. said that he is willing to do “whatever it takes to eliminate trade with the United States” and he has “ no interest in ever going back to the United States even for a visit.”

Sonja K. said that they have “bought Canadian products wherever possible” and has not “travelled to the U.S.” since Trump took office.

“Definitely will never buy any American products or travel to States, we support our country and government,” said reader Annie S.

“My husband and I are both determined to buy more Canadian! Even though we are seniors, we are willing to pay higher prices or change brands in order to support the country’s response to Trump’s trade war. And that includes no longer crossing the border and spending our Canadian dollars on American goods,” said Leni V.

For some readers, they say they would be willing to Buy Canadian but worry Canadian consumers will likely face higher prices as a result of new counter-tariffs.

“I would be, but only if Canadian companies and food stores do not put higher prices on Canadian goods made here and say because of tariffs the cost is higher. If Carney was to gives Canadians the item that Trump is placing tariffs on, so that Canadians know what products not to buy. On the energy liquid gas and hydro front stop sending it the states and use it to keep gas prices and hydro cost lower for Canadians,” said Brad N.

Darrell B. suggested that the counter tariffs are “only going to destroy the economy even more” and “make life even more unaffordable.”

“Counter tariffs are really the Canadian government telling its citizens that they will bear the brunt of the tariffs in order for Canada to stand up to the US. Both tariffs are counterproductive….smaller Canadian firms will suffer and probably close if this continues,” said reader Tom A.

Reader Rod C. pointed out that the U.S. “is Canada’s single most valuable trading partner” and said the country should “never jeopardize this relationship.”

“I would not be willing to pay more for necessary items. Groceries and clothing are on that list,” he added.

There was, however, a minority of respondents who said they would not be interested in paying a higher price and are less determined to Buy Canadian.

“No I will not buy Canadian unless it is the lowest priced item on the shelf. With the rising costs, we as Canadians have to support our selves and having to pay more for items is not what I voted for,” said Dale C.

“I definitely do not agree with Carneys position. He is making things worse with the U.S.,” said Winnie D.

The Government of Canada launched the Buy Canadian policy in December 2025, to protect and prioritize Canadian workers and industries while strengthening Canada’s domestic economy.

The changes were created to help create a strong Canadian supply chain by prioritizing Canadian suppliers and Canadian-made goods and services wherever possible.

They also aim to help Canadian industries become more self-sufficient and resilient to changes in the global economy.

That came after the movement gained traction across the country in early 2025 shortly after Trump was inaugurated and imposed the first rounds of his tariffs on multiple sectors of the Canadian economy.

—With files from The Associated Press

stories.title: Ontario Premier Doug Ford set to shuffle his cabinet today
stories.summary: is shuffling his cabinet today, with at least a few people set to move around as he has three posts to fill.
stories.author: The Canadian Press
stories.content:
TORONTO - Ontario Premier Doug Ford made several changes to his cabinet Thursday, including adding an artificial intelligence portfolio and moving embattled minister David Piccini from labour to infrastructure.

Sept. 10, 2026

Updated at 3:25 p.m.

New subscriber benefit!

Copied to clipboard

A gifted article has been claimed.

Out of gifts for the month

Unfortunately you've used all of your gifts this month. Your counter will reset on the first day of next month.

Darren Calabrese/The Canadian Press file photo[](http://www.thestar.com/news/ontario/premier-doug-ford-set-to-shuffle-his-cabinet-today/article_97012364-9e09-56f6-85cc-33ffdfdcd95e.html)

By Allison Jones and Liam Casey The Canadian Press

Piccini is under investigation by the integrity commissioner after the auditor general raised questions about his handling of the $2.5-billion Skills Development Fund. Ford has defended Piccini and the success of the fund and framed the move Thursday as a positive one.

“I changed, I think it was nine ministers, so it’s a combination of moving people around, getting a fresh outlook, a fresh start within new ministries,” he said.

ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW

Who’s downloading photos of your kid at dance competitions?

“I put a lot of thought into it, and I think for any premier, myself, in the future or in the past, I think the toughest position you’re in is when you have to pick and choose who’s going to be in cabinet.”

There are 37 people in Ford’s cabinet, including eight associate minister roles. After Ford became premier in 2018 he made good on a promise to deliver a leaner cabinet, with 21 people, but it has steadily grown over his years in power.

NDP Leader Marit Stiles said Ford should have taken the opportunity to drop Piccini from cabinet entirely.

“Instead of accountability, the premier just rewarded him with another job,” she wrote in a statement. “This is ridiculous. His track record shows he can’t be trusted with public dollars and contracts.”

Kinga Surma, who previously served as the minister of infrastructure, is now the Treasury Board president, a role left vacant after Caroline Mulroney resigned earlier this year.

Trevor Jones, who had served in the agriculture portfolio, is the new labour minister, and Sam Oosterhoff moves from an associate minister role to fill the agriculture job.

Zee Hamid, who was also previously in an associate minister role, becomes the new minister of tourism, culture and gaming, after Stan Cho resigned from the job as he came under fire for spending $16,000 in Toronto hotel stays despite living in the city.

Brian Saunderson, a former Olympic rower, enters cabinet to become the new minister of sport, a portfolio left vacant after Neil Lumsden retired last month.

Among the other changes, Ford dropped the associate minister of auto theft and bail reform role he created two years ago, saying its mandate has been fulfilled, and has added an associate minister of artificial intelligence adoption.

“We’re going to start focusing on AI,” he said. “We’re going to be graduating over 17,000 AI graduates. That’s on top of the 94,000 STEM graduates that we graduate every single year.”

Ford named Vijay Thanigasalam to that role, moving him from the role of associate minister of mental health and addictions.

In addition to Saunderson, two other new faces join cabinet, with Michelle Cooper serving in the mental health associate portfolio, and Matthew Rae becoming associate minister of energy-intensive industries.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 10, 2026.

The Canadian Press

stories.title: Ontario Premier Doug Ford to shuffle cabinet Thursday
stories.summary: Office positions the move as a response to Canada’s trade war with the U.S.
stories.author: Laura Stone, Jeff Gray
stories.content:
Ontario Premier Doug Ford shuffled his cabinet Thursday, moving David Piccini, who is under an ethics investigation, from labour to infrastructure, naming Kinga Surma as Treasury Board president and switching other members of his front bench.

The shuffle, which involved nine members, was positioned by Mr. Ford’s office as a response to the trade war with U.S. President Donald Trump. But opposition parties dismissed the changes as merely cosmetic.

“This is a good team for our plan to fight the tariffs, fight President Trump,” Mr. Ford told reporters at Queen’s Park. “I’m 100 per cent zoned in on the tariffs and on President Trump.”

Some of the changes announced were spurred by recent resignations from Mr. Ford’s cabinet. Ms. Surma, formerly infrastructure minister, will take over as Treasury Board president from Caroline Mulroney, who resigned as both a minister and MPP in June.

The Premier moved Mr. Piccini – who is facing an ethics probe – from the Labour Ministry to infrastructure, a large role overseeing megaprojects and billions in spending. Integrity Commissioner Cathryn Motherwell is investigating whether Mr. Piccini contravened the rules that govern MPPs in his handling of a controversial $2.5-billion skills training fund. The report has not yet been released.

The new cabinet will be in the legislature when the fall session begins on Oct. 27, after an extended summer break. The government has faced criticism from opposition parties for the long recess but Mr. Ford has said it was necessary to avoid interfering with municipal elections on Oct. 26. And he made it clear Thursday that he has no intention of bringing the legislature back earlier.

“We get so much more done when we aren’t in the house,” he said.

Other top ministers in finance, education, energy and health remain unchanged.

Mr. Ford defended his decision to keep Mr. Piccini on the front bench, calling the portfolio change a “natural move” from labour, where the minister oversaw the training of tens of thousands of workers.

Trevor Jones, previously agriculture minister, becomes Minister of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development. Sam Oosterhoff, formerly the associate minister of energy, becomes Agriculture Minister.

The three new faces in cabinet are Brian Saunderson, Michelle Cooper and Matthew Rae.

Mr. Saunderson, a former Olympic rower, becomes Sports Minister, taking over from Neil Lumsden, who resigned earlier this summer.

Ms. Cooper becomes associate minister of mental health and addictions, and Mr. Rae is associate minister of energy-intensive industries, which is part of the Ministry of Energy and Mines.

Zee Hamid, formerly the associate minister of auto theft and bail reform, becomes Minister of Tourism, Culture and Gaming. He takes over the portfolio from Toronto MPP Stan Cho, who resigned from Mr. Ford’s cabinet in July after it was revealed he billed thousands in local hotel stays in recent years.

The government said it eliminated Mr. Hamid’s previous post because its mandate “has been fulfilled,” pointing to stronger bail compliance rules and better tools for police to keep repeat offenders behind bars.

Vijay Thanigasalam takes on the new role of associate minister of artificial intelligence adoption, which is part of the Ministry of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade. The government said the role is being created “to ensure Ontario remains at the forefront of responsible AI adoption.”

The changes come on the heels of three by-elections held last week, which saw Mr. Ford’s PCs retain the two seats they held before the votes were called. The results followed months of controversy for the Premier, including over his aborted decision to buy a $28.9-million private jet. But in recent weeks, Mr. Ford saw his poll numbers rebound after the escalation of the trade war – and an exchange of public insults with Mr. Trump.

Opposition MPPs dismissed the shuffle as window dressing.

The NDP’s Kristyn Wong-Tam said moving Mr. Piccini from labour to infrastructure was an attempt to distract from the ethics investigation.

“There seems to be no punishment for wrongdoing when a Ford cabinet minister does something egregious, mismanages public dollars,” the Toronto MPP said. “They simply get moved around to another cabinet post.”

Interim Liberal leader John Fraser said the shuffle does nothing to help workers facing tariff-induced job losses – and pointed to the fact that, with 37 ministers, Mr. Ford has maintained his record-sized cabinet.

“Ontarians were hoping for a plan today. They got a new seating chart,” Mr. Fraser said in a statement, calling Mr. Ford’s the “most bloated cabinet in Ontario’s history.”

The Premier moved Mr. Piccini – who is facing an ethics probe – from the Labour Ministry to infrastructure, a large role overseeing megaprojects and billions in spending. Integrity Commissioner Cathryn Motherwell is investigating whether Mr. Piccini contravened the rules that govern MPPs in his handling of a controversial $2.5-billion skills training fund. The report has not yet been released.

The new cabinet will be in the legislature when the fall session begins on Oct. 27, after an extended summer break. The government has faced criticism from opposition parties for the long recess but Mr. Ford has said it was necessary to avoid interfering with municipal elections on Oct. 26. And he made it clear Thursday that he has no intention of bringing the legislature back earlier.

content_blocks.text: “We get so much more done when we aren’t in the house,” he said.
Other top ministers in finance, education, energy and health remain unchanged.

Mr. Ford defended his decision to keep Mr. Piccini on the front bench, calling the portfolio change a “natural move” from labour, where the minister oversaw the training of tens of thousands of workers.

content_blocks.text: Trevor Jones, previously agriculture minister, becomes Minister of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development. Sam Oosterhoff, formerly the associate minister of energy, becomes Agriculture Minister.
The three new faces in cabinet are Brian Saunderson, Michelle Cooper and Matthew Rae.
Mr. Saunderson, a former Olympic rower, becomes Sports Minister, taking over from Neil Lumsden, who resigned earlier this summer.
Ms. Cooper becomes associate minister of mental health and addictions, and Mr. Rae is associate minister of energy-intensive industries, which is part of the Ministry of Energy and Mines.

Zee Hamid, formerly the associate minister of auto theft and bail reform, becomes Minister of Tourism, Culture and Gaming. He takes over the portfolio from Toronto MPP Stan Cho, who resigned from Mr. Ford’s cabinet in July after it was revealed he billed thousands in local hotel stays in recent years.

Vijay Thanigasalam takes on the new role of associate minister of artificial intelligence adoption, which is part of the Ministry of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade. The government said the role is being created “to ensure Ontario remains at the forefront of responsible AI adoption.”

The changes come on the heels of three by-elections held last week, which saw Mr. Ford’s PCs retain the two seats they held before the votes were called. The results followed months of controversy for the Premier, including over his aborted decision to buy a $28.9-million private jet. But in recent weeks, Mr. Ford saw his poll numbers rebound after the escalation of the trade war – and an exchange of public insults with Mr. Trump.

“Ontarians were hoping for a plan today. They got a new seating chart,” Mr. Fraser said in a statement, calling Mr. Ford’s the “most bloated cabinet in Ontario’s history.”

stories.title: Deep River, Ont., under shelter-in-place order as police investigate stabbing
stories.summary: Deep River - Residents in a town northwest of Petawawa, Ont., have been asked to shelter in place as police look for a suspect in a reported stabbing.
stories.author: The Canadian Press
stories.content:
Police say officers responded to the area of McElligott Drive in Deep River, where a victim was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries Wednesday afternoon.

Officers issued a notice urging residents to stay indoors with all doors and windows locked as the search for a suspect continued.

ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW

Who’s downloading photos of your kid at dance competitions?

Officials said Thursday morning that the town’s facilities and a school were closed, students in another school were kept indoors all day and school buses were cancelled.

In an afternoon update, police said the shelter-in-place order has been lifted, but they didn’t say whether a suspect was taken into custody.

Police say they will have an increased presence in the area as the investigation continues.

Investigators are asking residents to be vigilant and report any suspicious activities immediately.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published on Sept. 10, 2026.

The Canadian Press

OTTAWA - Two RCMP disaster victim identification specialists are in Kathmandu to assist Canadian officials already in the region in response to flash floods along the Nepal-China border.

Canada is assisting international efforts to locate survivors after devastating floods on Aug. 26 killed more than 1,100 people and left roughly 4,400 missing in the region along the Nepal-China border.

In Kathmandu, police have buried dozens of unidentified bodies in trenches because there are too many to keep or identify individually.

stories.title: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to meet with Carney and cabinet in Banff
stories.summary: is set to meet with Prime Minister Mark Carney and his cabinet Thursday.
stories.author: Christopher Nardi
stories.content:
Zelenskyy met Carney and his cabinet Thursday in Alberta during a previously unannounced two-day visit to Canada

Ottawa — Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada’s military needs “millions” of drones for the modern battlefield but only has 2,000, as he signed a new deal with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to boost the country’s production and share them with Ukraine.

During a joint announcement with Zelenskyy, Carney announced a new Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace (Ddim) that he said would give Canadian government agencies and their allies “privileged access” to roughly 400 Canadian drone suppliers.

The prime minister said the new deal aims to increase Canada’s drone production tenfold in coming years.

“ This is a key part of our plan to build industrial capacity here in Canada to produce millions of drones within the next two years, a nd today’s contracts will increase the number of drones available to the cap tenfold,” Carney said.

“Importantly, one third of all the drones we manufacture will go to support Ukraine’s defence of its homeland,” he added.

Carney and Zelenskyy also signed a declaration committing to a future 100-year partnership in fields such as energy, security, defence and critical minerals. Carney also promised Ukraine over $400 million in loan guarantees to help the Eastern European country purchase energy for the coming winter.

Zelenskyy also said this signature was the first step to another “big drone deal” coming between Canada and Ukraine.

“Thirty per cent of these drones will go to Ukraine immediately to battle. Immediately to our people, our soldiers , to save our children, our families ,” he said.

The Ukrainian president landed in Calgary with his wife Olena Zelenska on Wednesday evening, where he was greeted by Canadian and European dignitaries as well as Foreign Minister Anita Anand.

He will meet with Carney in Calgary and then travel to Banff, Alta., where he is expected to speak to cabinet during its two-day retreat beginning Thursday. The Ukrainian president then plans to travel to Toronto and North Bay before leaving Canada on Friday.

As is usual for Zelenskyy’s travel during his country’s ongoing war against Russia’s invasion in 2022, his visit was kept under wraps until his arrival.

“ Canada has been and remains one of our closest partners. We value all the support from Canadians and the decisions that help Ukraine stand strong and protect our people,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media while announcing his visit.

“ The main focus will be on supporting Ukraine in protecting our skies and preparing for the winter. We will discuss how to strengthen our resilience, support our people, and ensure that Ukraine has the capabilities it needs to defend itself,”

In a separate statement, Carney said the focus of the visit was “deepening defence, economic, and energy cooperation.”

“It will also address the human cost of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and build on the strong people-to-people ties that connect our countries,” Carney said in a statement.

The prime minister and Zelenskyy are expected to jointly address the media just before 1 p.m. ET.

stories.title: Carney to hold joint press conference with Ukraine’s Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney says the meeting will focus on the countries' shared priorities, including deepening defence, economic and energy co-operation.
stories.author: Bill Graveland
stories.content:
Canada and Ukraine are deepening cooperation in key areas such as defence, critical minerals and intelligence sharing, Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a joint statement.

“Meeting at a moment of global rupture, the leaders reaffirmed their intention to build a new order founded on trust, rooted in shared values, and underpinned by the strength and determination to uphold them,” a joint statement from the two read.

Both countries agreed to establish “a long-term defence industrial partnership,” including the joint production of counter-drone capabilities.

Canada and Ukraine also agreed to ensure “safe and secure navigation in the Black Sea,” a key shipping route for food grains for markets across the world.

Carney and Zelenskyy signed a “Declaration for a Hundred Year Partnership” between Canada and Ukraine.

Ottawa and Kyiv “will codify a long-term framework for cooperation across defence and security, trade and investment, reconstruction, energy, critical minerals, and technology,” Carney said.

The federal government will also ramp up its defence drone production, with a plan to “produce millions of drones within the next two years,” he added.

Based on a model employed by the Ukrainian government, Canada will set up a “national drone market place,” which will give access to the Canadian Armed Forces to around 400 Canadian drone suppliers.

“One-third of all the drones we manufacture will go to support Ukraine’s defence of its homeland,” Carney said.

Zelenskyy last visited Canada in December, stopping in Halifax, amid efforts to end the war that Russia started in 2014 and escalated with a full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Kyiv has suffered a barrage of Russian airstrikes in recent months, and Ukraine has pleaded for more air defence support from its allies.

Since 2022, Canada has pledged $6.5 billion in military assistance for Ukraine running through to 2029.

“Canada remains steadfast in our commitment to support Ukraine’s defence, recovery, and reconstruction,” Carney said in a statement Wednesday.

–with files from Canadian Press
